arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Bursch argued sex and transgender status are independent concepts. He stated equal treatment does not mean treating men as women.
General Francisco argued the case is not close textually. He addressed Justice Gorsuch's comment about the textual nature of the case.
Mr. Cole stated Aimee Stephens was a valued employee for six years. He noted she was fired after telling her boss she identifies as a woman.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on October 8, 2019.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The funeral home wants to keep its bathroom rules. It argues sex and gender identity are separate.
The EEOC wants to protect transgender workers. It argues discrimination based on gender identity is sex discrimination.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The funeral home argues sex and transgender status are independent concepts. It claims equal treatment does not mean treating men as women.
The EEOC argues the case is not close textually. It claims a reasonable person would be harmed by such rules.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Sotomayor asked what law guides judges in balancing these interests. She noted the question becomes inevitable if the employer wins.
Justice Gorsuch asked if a reasonable person would be harmed by bathroom rules. He suggested this might be the core issue.
